name: vintage_aware_incremental
description: Store every observation under an explicit vintage key in an append-only table and maintain the serving state incrementally for only the cells that the H6C lineage marks as affected by each arriving release.

input.workload: the same 38-observation real-revision workload used by B0, B1, and B2

store.write_action: INSERT the arriving release rows only

serving.maintenance: MERGE only the resolved rows of dirty cells after each arrival

impact_analysis.dirty_cell_rule: cells reached from the arriving observation nodes through exact H6C lineage edges

equivalence.check: incremental serving state equals a full recomputation from the store after every arrival

reproducibility.snapshot_policy: expire both B3 tables to their latest snapshot after the run; historical reads use the vintage key only
reproducibility.as_of_reconstruction: latest stored vintage per cell whose resolution key is not later than the requested release
reproducibility.as_of_must_equal: B1 logical snapshot states on every H6 observation column

rebuild_policy: drop and recreate only the two B3 experiment tables before a complete run
invariants: the store never updates or deletes a committed observation row
each (cell_id, vintage_id) pair and each observation_id occurs once in the store
dirty cells are derived from exact H6C lineage edges and equal the arriving observations' cell_id values
only dirty cells are recomputed; untouched cells keep their earlier resolved row
after every arrival the incremental serving state equals a full recomputation from the store
the final serving state equals the B0 and B1 latest-vintage states on all H6 observation columns
the as-of reconstruction for every release equals the corresponding B1 snapshot state
all 38 H6 observations are addressable by (cell_id, vintage_id) after table snapshots are expired
the resolved serving state does not depend on the arrival order of releases
